description: Plain-language profile of every law in the store: what it is, how it can reach construction prices, and how it is identified. Written by hand from the official titles; 'channel' is the main route to construction prices. 'note' flags known data issues.

channels.materials: Cost or availability of building materials
channels.building requirements: What a building must meet (energy, safety, products)
channels.planning: Where and how much may be built

law_32024R3110.title: Construction Products Regulation (recast), Regulation (EU) 2024/3110
law_32024R3110.summary: Sets the EU rules for placing construction products on the market: harmonised technical specifications, declarations of performance and conformity, CE marking, and new duties on environmental performance and digital product information. It replaces Regulation (EU) No 305/2011 in stages.
law_32024R3110.price_link: Testing, certification and environmental declarations add to producers' costs, which reach material prices.

law_32024L1275.title: Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (recast), Directive (EU) 2024/1275
law_32024L1275.summary: Requires new buildings to be zero-emission buildings (public buildings first), tightens energy-performance rules for renovations, introduces renovation passports and minimum performance standards for non-residential buildings, and phases out fossil-fuel boilers. Member States transpose it into national law (in Germany mainly the GEG).
law_32024L1275.price_link: Higher energy standards change what has to be built (insulation, heat pumps, solar readiness), raising the cost per building.

law_32023R0956.title: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, Regulation (EU) 2023/956
law_32023R0956.summary: Puts a carbon price on imports of cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen, matching the EU emissions trading price. Reporting started in October 2023; payments are phased in from 2026 as free allocation under the EU ETS is phased out.
law_32023R0956.price_link: Imported cement, steel and aluminium become more expensive as the CBAM factor rises; domestic producers lose free allowances on the same schedule.

law_32023L0959.title: Revision of the EU Emissions Trading System, Directive (EU) 2023/959
law_32023L0959.summary: Amends the EU ETS Directive 2003/87/EC: a steeper cap, the phase-out of free allocation alongside CBAM, and a separate emissions trading system (ETS2) for fuels used in buildings and road transport, planned from 2027 (postponement to 2028 possible).
law_32023L0959.price_link: Raises carbon costs for cement, steel and energy-intensive materials, and through ETS2 for heating and diesel fuel.

law_32023D0852.title: Market Stability Reserve amendment, Decision (EU) 2023/852
law_32023D0852.summary: Adjusts the operation of the market stability reserve, which takes surplus allowances off the EU ETS market to support the carbon price.
law_32023D0852.price_link: Indirect: affects the carbon price that energy-intensive material producers pay.

law_32015L1814.title: Market Stability Reserve for the EU ETS, Decision (EU) 2015/1814
law_32015L1814.summary: Established the market stability reserve of the EU emissions trading system, which absorbs surplus allowances.
law_32015L1814.price_link: Indirect: supports the carbon price paid by producers of cement, steel and energy.
law_32015L1814.note: Stored under the identifier 32015L1814; the official CELEX number of a decision is 32015D1814.

law_32021R1119.title: European Climate Law, Regulation (EU) 2021/1119
law_32021R1119.summary: Makes climate neutrality by 2050 and a net reduction of at least 55% in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 legally binding for the EU.
law_32021R1119.price_link: Sets the targets that the ETS revision, CBAM and building rules implement.

law_32020R0852.title: EU Taxonomy Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2020/852
law_32020R0852.summary: Defines which economic activities count as environmentally sustainable, including technical criteria for constructing and renovating buildings.
law_32020R0852.price_link: Indirect: financing terms can favour buildings that meet the criteria.

law_32022L2464.title: Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, Directive (EU) 2022/2464
law_32022L2464.summary: Requires large and listed companies to report on sustainability under European reporting standards, with external assurance.
law_32022L2464.price_link: Indirect: reporting costs and pressure on suppliers for emissions data.

law_32019R2088.title: Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2019/2088
law_32019R2088.summary: Requires financial market participants to disclose how they consider sustainability risks and impacts in their products.
law_32019R2088.price_link: Indirect: affects how property and construction investments are financed.

law_32018L2002.title: Amendment of the Energy Efficiency Directive, Directive (EU) 2018/2002
law_32018L2002.summary: Amends Directive 2012/27/EU with a 2030 energy efficiency target and rules on metering and billing of heating.
law_32018L2002.price_link: Indirect: implemented in Germany through the GEG and related rules.

law_32018L2001.title: Renewable Energy Directive (recast), Directive (EU) 2018/2001
law_32018L2001.summary: Sets the EU renewable energy target for 2030 and requires Member States to promote renewable energy for heating and cooling, including in buildings.
law_32018L2001.price_link: Requirements for renewable heating in new buildings (in Germany through the GEG) change building costs.

law_32018L0844.title: Amendment of the Energy Performance of Buildings Directive, Directive (EU) 2018/844
law_32018L0844.summary: Amends the EPBD 2010 with long-term renovation strategies, building automation and electric-vehicle charging requirements.
law_32018L0844.price_link: Adds technical requirements to new buildings and major renovations.

law_32018R1999.title: Governance of the Energy Union and Climate Action, Regulation (EU) 2018/1999
law_32018R1999.summary: Requires national energy and climate plans and progress reports from Member States.
law_32018R1999.price_link: Indirect: planning framework for national climate and energy measures.

law_32012L0027.title: Energy Efficiency Directive, Directive 2012/27/EU
law_32012L0027.summary: Common framework of energy efficiency measures, including renovation of public buildings and energy audits for large companies.
law_32012L0027.price_link: Indirect: implemented in Germany partly through the GEG.

law_32010L0031.title: Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (recast), Directive 2010/31/EU
law_32010L0031.summary: Introduced minimum energy performance requirements, energy performance certificates and the nearly zero-energy standard for new buildings from 2021. Replaced by the 2024 recast.
law_32010L0031.price_link: The nearly zero-energy standard shaped German energy rules for new buildings (EnEV, now GEG).

law_32011L0092.title: Environmental Impact Assessment Directive, Directive 2011/92/EU
law_32011L0092.summary: Requires an assessment of the environmental effects of certain public and private projects before they are approved.
law_32011L0092.price_link: Adds time and cost to larger projects; implemented in Germany partly through the BauGB.

law_32014L0052.title: Amendment of the EIA Directive, Directive 2014/52/EU
law_32014L0052.summary: Strengthens the environmental impact assessment with new topics such as climate change and disaster risk.
law_32014L0052.price_link: Indirect: assessment duties for larger projects.

law_32001L0042.title: Strategic Environmental Assessment Directive, Directive 2001/42/EC
law_32001L0042.summary: Requires environmental assessment of plans and programmes, such as land-use plans, before adoption.
law_32001L0042.price_link: Indirect: affects how quickly building land is designated.

law_32013L0017.title: Adaptation of environmental directives on the accession of Croatia, Directive 2013/17/EU
law_32013L0017.summary: Technical amendments to several environmental directives (including habitats and birds) following Croatia's accession to the EU.
law_32013L0017.price_link: None directly; stored because German planning law cites it.

law_31992L0043.title: Habitats Directive, Council Directive 92/43/EEC
law_31992L0043.summary: Protects natural habitats and wild species through the Natura 2000 network; plans and projects that may affect a protected site need an appropriate assessment.
law_31992L0043.price_link: Can delay or restrict building on land near protected sites.

law_32009L0147.title: Birds Directive, Directive 2009/147/EC
law_32009L0147.summary: Protects all wild bird species and their habitats, including special protection areas that are part of Natura 2000.
law_32009L0147.price_link: Can restrict building in or near protected areas.

law_32024R1781.title: Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2024/1781
law_32024R1781.summary: Framework for setting ecodesign requirements (durability, recycled content, carbon footprint) for almost all physical products, with a digital product passport.
law_32024R1781.price_link: Future requirements for products such as steel, cement or insulation could raise production costs.

law_de_geg.title: Buildings Energy Act (Gebäudeenergiegesetz, GEG)
law_de_geg.summary: Sets energy requirements for new and existing buildings in Germany: maximum primary energy demand, insulation standards, energy certificates and, since 2024, the rule that new heating systems run on at least 65% renewable energy (phased in). It implements the EU buildings and efficiency directives.
law_de_geg.price_link: Determines insulation, heating and technical equipment, a large share of the cost of a new home.

law_de_behg.title: Fuel Emissions Trading Act (Brennstoffemissionshandelsgesetz, BEHG)
law_de_behg.summary: Puts a national CO2 price on heating and transport fuels from 2021, at fixed prices rising each year and then in a price corridor, until the EU's ETS2 takes over. The prices set in the law are stored as a policy series.
law_de_behg.price_link: Raises the cost of diesel for construction machinery and of fuels used to make and transport materials.

law_de_bbaug.title: Federal Building Code (Baugesetzbuch, BauGB)
law_de_bbaug.summary: Germany's planning law: land-use and development plans, when building is allowed, pre-emption rights, and environmental assessment in planning. It implements the EU habitats, birds, EIA and SEA directives.
law_de_bbaug.price_link: Determines how much building land is available and how long approval takes.

law_de_baunvo.title: Land Use Ordinance (Baunutzungsverordnung, BauNVO)
law_de_baunvo.summary: Defines the types of building areas (residential, mixed, commercial) and how densely they may be built on, used in every development plan.
law_de_baunvo.price_link: Density limits affect how many homes fit on a plot, and so land cost per home.

law_de_hoai_2013.title: Fee Structure for Architects and Engineers (Honorarordnung, HOAI)
law_de_hoai_2013.summary: Fee tables and service phases for architects and engineers. Since 2021 the fees are guidance only and can be agreed freely, after the European Court of Justice ruled the binding minimum and maximum rates unlawful in 2019.
law_de_hoai_2013.price_link: Design and engineering fees are part of total building costs, though not of the construction price index.

law_de_ustg_1980.title: VAT Act (Umsatzsteuergesetz, UStG)
law_de_ustg_1980.summary: German value added tax. Construction work is taxed at the standard rate, 19% since 2007 (16% from July to December 2020). The rate history is stored and used by the forecast.
law_de_ustg_1980.price_link: The target index includes VAT, so every rate change moves it directly.

law_de_aentg_2009.title: Posted Workers Act (Arbeitnehmer-Entsendegesetz, AEntG)
law_de_aentg_2009.summary: Allows collectively agreed minimum wages to be made binding for all employers in a sector, including those posting workers from abroad. Several building trades (for example roofing and scaffolding) have such minimum wages.
law_de_aentg_2009.price_link: Sets a wage floor in the trades it covers, feeding labour costs.
